newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA OIL RIG IN FIELD, PUMPING SEEN MID-APRIL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA OIL RIG IN FIELD, PUMPING SEEN MID-APRIL.

text.p: South African oil exploration and production firm Soekor said on Tuesday pumping at the country's first offshore oilfield was likely to start in the middle of April.
Andre van Niekerk, a spokesman for Soekor, told Reuters its semi-submersible rig, the Orca, was in position in the Oribi oil field 90 miles southwest of Mossel Bay.

However, the diving support vessel, which is installing the rig's sub-sea pipeline and which has been in the field for the past week, was struggling to do some of its work due to poor weather conditions and high waves.

"When (the vessel) does more of the sensitive work where pipes need to be put in, which have buoyancy models on them, it moves around too much and it is too dangerous to do the work," van Niekerk said.
Asked when production would start, van Niekerk, reiterating a statement released by Soekor last month, said:

"It was originally the end of March, but we know it won't be the end of the March anymore. But with the finicky weather we are having at the moment it is just not possible to set a definite date. Middle April, somewhere there, is how it looks at the moment."
The start of production has on been plagued by numerous delays, mainly due to bad weather.

First sales of oil from Oribi will be in May. Soekor and minority partner Energy Africa plan to market oil from Oribi on a tanker-by-tanker basis with the crude going to local refineries in Cape Town or Durban.
